title: Dear Su Yen: Letters to a Daughter
author: Khoo Seok Wan
target_audience: Readers interested in Asian memoirs and personal letters
Parents seeking reflections on raising daughters
Those curious about family dynamics in multicultural contexts
core_themes: Passing on life advice and wisdom
Love and longing across distance and time
primary_purpose: To capture the intimate, heartfelt advice and reflections of a parent writing to his daughter, sharing family memories, cultural values, and personal experiences for her future guidance.

structure_format.organization: A collection of sequential letters from father to daughter, each with a thematic focus
features: Reflections on cultural change and family history

key_concepts_lessons: Importance of maintaining family bonds even across distance
Transitioning traditions and values to a new generation
Learning from successes and failures of parents
Balancing individual identity and familial expectation
notable_features: Epistolary format—real letters to a daughter
Blend of practical advice and emotional support
cultural_historical_context: The book offers an authentic glimpse into contemporary Singaporean family life, exploring how traditional values are adapted and passed down in a rapidly changing society.
reception_impact: Gained acclaim for its emotional honesty and cultural resonance
Appreciated among readers seeking genuine narratives of parenting and identity
Used in academic discussions of epistolary literature and Asian memoirs
comparable_titles: Letters to My Daughter by Maya Angelou
Dear Girls: Intimate Tales, Untold Secrets & Advice by Ali Wong
Tuesdays with Morrie by Mitch Albom (for wisdom-sharing tone)
